learningObjectives: Use Pulse to post, view, and reply to messages with case stakeholders and teams
Explain how developers and users each access Pulse
Configure Tags to classify Pulse messages and find related Cases
Recognize Pulse email notification triggers and reply-by-email behavior

elements.description: Pega's built-in messaging system. Users post, view, and reply in the Pulse Activity Feed — directed to specific users, team members, or Case stakeholders. Example: a CSR posts once to update every Case participant on a claim's status.

elements.text: Pega's Pulse collaboration is like a digital sticky-note wall inside each case: any team member can post a message, @mention a colleague, or attach a file — all permanently linked to that specific case. The conversation stays with the work, not scattered across disconnected email threads that someone has to manually reassemble later.

elements.description: DEVELOPERS: click 'Toggle developer collaboration' in the App Studio header to open the Developer Collaboration pane. USERS: access Pulse via a Pulse Widget added to the portal Navigation bar or embedded in the Case work area.

Reply to a Pulse message with or without a comment. Users opt into email notifications for @-mentions, likes, replies in conversations they participated in, or posts to Cases they follow. Email replies appear as Pulse comments without login.

elements.caption: Three collaboration tools: Pulse for internal in-case discussion, Tags for categorizing and grouping related cases, Send Email for automated external communication.

elements.description: Descriptive words or phrases ASSOCIATED WITH A PULSE MESSAGE that categorize messages so users can quickly find information to resolve a Case. Add a tag by typing # followed by a word/phrase WITHOUT SPACES.
Lists tags relevant to a Case. Each tag is a link — clicking it shows all Cases sharing that tag. Added to the Full Case Page (not the Navigation bar, where the Pulse widget lives).

elements.title: Collaboration Tool Matcher

examPitfalls.title: Two ways to access Pulse
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Developers use the Toggle developer collaboration pane in App Studio; users use a Pulse widget on the portal Navigation bar.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Match the access path to the audience; the user Pulse widget must be configured by a developer.

examPitfalls.title: Pulse email notification triggers
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask when Pulse sends an email notification to a participant. Candidates say 'every time someone posts.' Pulse sends an email only when a user is specifically @mentioned — general posts do not trigger email notifications unless the user has opted in.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Know the four triggers; users can reply from the email without logging in.

examPitfalls.title: Reply with or without a comment
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks whether replying to a Pulse post requires typing a comment. Candidates say yes. Users can reply to a Pulse post either with a typed comment or by clicking a Like/emoji reaction — a comment is not required.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Remember that users can respond to a Pulse post with a typed comment or a reaction — a text comment is not required to acknowledge or respond.

examPitfalls.title: Tags use # and no spaces
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A tag is entered with the # symbol followed by a word/phrase with NO spaces; tags attach to Pulse messages.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Create a tag with #word or reuse a recent one.

examPitfalls.title: Tags widget is a clickable link
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask what happens when a user clicks a tag in the Tags widget. Candidates say 'nothing; tags are display-only.' Clicking a tag in the Tags widget opens a filtered view of all cases with that tag — tags are interactive navigation links.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the Tags widget on the full case page to navigate related Cases.

examPitfalls.title: Widget placement
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks where the Pulse widget can be placed. Candidates say 'only on the Case summary page.' The Pulse widget can be placed on any Case page or portal page — its placement is not restricted to the Case summary.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Know which Pulse widget belongs on the Case page vs. the portal page — placement determines which Case context the widget surfaces to the user.

examPitfalls.title: Cross-module connections
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions describe a user needing to see collaboration updates across multiple modules. Candidates say Pulse is per-Case only. Pulse notifications and tags can surface in any portal that includes the relevant widget — cross-module visibility depends on portal configuration.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: → SA-M17 (Sending emails): Send email is external; Pulse is in-Case collaboration. → SA-M11 (User guidance): Pulse complements status/instructions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A CSR must update every participant on an automobile claim about its payment status in one place inside the Case. Which tool fits?

options.text: Pulse — post a single message in the Case's activity feed to the participants
A Send email Step to each participant individually
A Tag on the Case
An Access Role update

practiceQuiz.hint: In-Case messaging posted to Case stakeholders and participants is called Pulse.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Pulse posts a single message to Case participants in the activity feed. B is external email, not in-Case collaboration. C is for classification, not messaging. D governs permissions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega developer working in App Studio wants to read and respond to collaboration messages posted on a Claims Case by a business analyst. The developer asks how to access the Pulse collaboration feature from within App Studio. How does an application developer access Pulse in App Studio?

options.text: Click 'Toggle developer collaboration' in the App Studio header to open the Developer collaboration pane
Add a Pulse widget to the Navigation bar
Open Admin Studio's collaboration console
Enable a Data Page that streams messages

practiceQuiz.hint: Developers use the collaboration pane in App Studio.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Developers use the Toggle developer collaboration icon to open the Developer collaboration pane. B is how USERS access Pulse. C and D are not Pulse access methods.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is explaining Pega's collaboration features to a project team and is asked how an end user gets access to Pulse in their portal. How does an end user get Pulse added to their portal?

options.text: A developer adds a Pulse widget to the portal Navigation bar (or embeds it in a Case's work area)
Users automatically see Pulse everywhere with no configuration
Users open the Developer collaboration pane
Users install a browser extension

practiceQuiz.hint: User access = Pulse widget on the Navigation bar.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Users access Pulse via a Pulse widget that a developer adds to the Navigation bar. B is wrong because the widget must be configured. C is the developer path. D is not a Pega mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO events can trigger an email notification about a Pulse message?

options.text: Someone @-mentions the user or one of their teams
Someone posts a Pulse message to a Case the user follows
The user's password is about to expire
A Ruleset is locked

practiceQuiz.hint: Which two specific Pulse interaction types trigger an email notification to a user?
practiceQuiz.rationale: @-mentions and posts to a followed Case are Pulse email triggers (along with likes and comments in participated conversations). C and D are unrelated to Pulse notifications.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A user receives a Pulse email notification. Can they respond without logging into Pega?

options.text: Yes — they can reply from the email, and the reply appears as a comment on the top message
No — they must log in to the portal to reply
Only if they are an application developer
Only by phone to the administrator

practiceQuiz.hint: Determine whether Pulse email notifications allow a direct reply without logging into Pega.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Users can reply directly from the email without logging in; the reply is added as a comment on the top message. B, C, D contradict the email-reply capability.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is training new team members on Pega's collaboration tools and explains how to tag Pulse messages for searchability. How do you add the tag 'innovation' to a Pulse message?

options.text: Type # followed by the word with no spaces (e.g., #innovation), or pick a recently used tag
Type @ followed by the word
Wrap the word in quotes
Add it as an Access Role

practiceQuiz.hint: Recall the exact syntax for adding a tag to a Pulse message — which character and spacing rule applies?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Tags are added with the # symbol followed by a word/phrase without spaces. B (@) is for mentioning users/teams. C and D are not how tags are created.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the Tags widget, what happens when a user clicks a tag?

options.text: A dialog opens listing the Cases tagged with that word or phrase — the tag acts as a link
The tag is deleted from the Case
A new Case is created with that tag
The application restarts to apply the tag

practiceQuiz.hint: A tag is a clickable link to tagged Cases.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Clicking a tag in the Tags widget opens a dialog listing all Cases tagged with that word/phrase. Options B, C, and D describe behaviors that tags do not perform.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Where does a developer add the Pulse widget versus the Tags widget?

options.text: Pulse widget → the portal Navigation bar; Tags widget → the full case page
Both widgets go only on the Navigation bar
Both widgets go only on the full case page
Neither can be added in App Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: Pulse = nav bar; Tags = full case page.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Pulse widget is added to the Navigation bar and the Tags widget to the full case page (both from App Studio). B, C, D misstate the placements/availability.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A CSR wants to ask a legal colleague a question without leaving the case UI or sending external email. Which Pega feature is designed for this?

options.text: Pulse — in-case messaging where team members can post messages, @mention colleagues, and attach files
Send Email shape — triggers automated email to the legal team from within the case process
Co-Browse — shares the CSR screen with the legal colleague for simultaneous viewing
Case Locking — assigns exclusive edit access to the legal colleague so they can add input

practiceQuiz.hint: Which tool enables inline case communication without external tools?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Pulse keeps all case-related communication attached to the case record. B sends external SMTP email with no automatic reply threading back to the case. C is for sharing screens with customers, not internal collaboration. D is a concurrency control mechanism, not a communication tool.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An operator @mentions @JaneSmith in a Pulse message. Jane receives a notification. Which statement is accurate?

options.text: The @mention triggered an in-app Pega notification for Jane — she can click it to navigate to the case
The @mention sent an external email to Jane's registered address with a link to the case
The @mention added Jane as a case collaborator, granting her write access to fields she did not previously have
The @mention created an assignment in Jane's worklist that blocks the case until she acknowledges it

practiceQuiz.hint: Think: what notification behavior does an @mention in Pulse trigger for the recipient?
practiceQuiz.rationale: @mention in Pulse sends an in-app notification (bell icon) linking Jane to the case. B is wrong because @mention triggers in-app notification, not external email by default. C is wrong because @mention does not grant permissions — those are controlled by Access Roles. D is wrong because @mention does not create a formal assignment or block the case.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer wants to display the case Pulse feed at the bottom of every case view so operators always see recent messages. How is this configured?

options.text: Add the Pulse section to the case view layout in App Studio — it renders the collaboration feed for the current case
Enable the Show Pulse toggle in Case Type settings to globally activate the feed for all cases
Install the Pulse module — collaboration requires a separate licensed add-on not included in base Pega Platform
Configure a Data Page to load Pulse messages via the Collaboration API and bind to a table control in the view

practiceQuiz.hint: How is the Pulse feed added to a case view?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Pulse section is added to the case view layout as a standard UI section. B is wrong because there is no single 'Show Pulse' toggle in Case Type settings. C is wrong because Pulse is built into Pega Platform. D is wrong because manually binding a Data Page is an unnecessary workaround.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A manager wants all Pulse messages from the past week searchable by keyword. Which statement is accurate?

options.text: Pulse messages are stored as case data and can be searched via case history views or Insights queries
Pulse messages are deleted after 24 hours and cannot be searched retroactively
Pulse messages are only visible to the author and @mentioned operators
Pulse messages are in a separate log table not accessible from the standard case UI or search tools

practiceQuiz.hint: Think: are Pulse messages persistent, searchable, and available to participants after posting?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Pulse messages are permanent case history data and persist as long as the case exists. B is wrong because they are not temporary. C is wrong because all operators with case access can see Pulse messages. D is wrong because Pulse data is part of the standard case history model.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is explaining the purpose of Tags in Pega Pulse. Which TWO statements correctly describe how Tags function?

options.text: Tags categorize Pulse messages so that related Cases and discussions can be grouped and filtered
Pulse Tags can be searched across Cases to surface all messages and Cases sharing the same tag
Adding a Tag to a Pulse message automatically creates a new Case linked to that tag
Pulse Tags replace Case Status as the primary mechanism for tracking Case progress in Pega

practiceQuiz.hint: Tags are for classification and discoverability of Pulse messages — they do not create Cases or replace status.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Pulse Tags allow users to categorize collaboration messages by topic, making it easy to filter related messages within and across Cases. Tags are also searchable, enabling users to find all Cases and Pulse messages that share a common tag. Tags do not create Cases or serve as a Case progress tracking mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer is configuring Pulse for a Claims application. Which TWO behaviors correctly describe how Pulse email notifications work in Pega?

options.text: Pega can send email notifications to Case participants when a new Pulse message is posted
Recipients can reply to a Pulse email notification and have their reply automatically appear as a Pulse message in the Case
Pulse email notifications are broadcast to all Pega operators in the application regardless of their participation in the Case
Pulse email notifications require a separate correspondence Ruleset to be imported from Pega Marketplace

practiceQuiz.hint: Pulse notifications go to Case participants — not all users — and reply-by-email posts back to the Case.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Pega Pulse sends email notifications to Case participants (followers and involved parties) when a new message is posted. Recipients can reply to the notification email and their reply will appear as a new Pulse message in the Case. Notifications are not broadcast to all operators, and no separate Ruleset import is required.

quickRecap.value: OOTB messaging: post/view/reply in the activity feed to users, teams, or Case/app stakeholders.
Developers: Toggle developer collaboration pane (App Studio). Users: Pulse widget on the Navigation bar.
Reply with/without a comment. Email triggers: @-mention · like · comment in participated convo · post to a followed Case. Reply from email without logging in.
Words/phrases on a Pulse message to classify/relate; add with # + word, NO spaces; create new or reuse recent.
Lists a Case's tags; each tag is a LINK to a dialog of tagged Cases; added to the full case page.
